Powered by Reelgood When the end credits roll on Paradise Season 2, Episode 7, jaws will be dropped, minds will be racing, questions will be burning, and “The Final Countdown” will truly be upon us. Paradise Season 2, Episode 7 spoilers ahead. With only one episode remaining in Season 2 of Dan Fogelman’s hit Hulu series, the finale has a lot of ground to cover before it leaves viewers on a painful hiatus ahead of Season 3. “The Final Countdown” saw Xavier (Sterling K. Brown) and Teri (Enuka Okuma) reunite and head to the Colorado Bunker. Jane (Nicole Brydon Bloom) and Gabriela’s (Sarah Shahi) tensions reached a climax. Robinson (Krys Marshall), Jeremy (Charlie Evans), and Anders (Erik Svedberg-Zelman) broke out of Paradise Prison and tampered with the bunker’s oxygen supply to force the doors open. Meanwhile, panicked leaders — worried about Link’s (Thomas Doherty) crew breaking in — put the bunker into full lockdown mode without Sinatra’s (Julianne Nicholson) permission. The conflicting commands led to a system failure, which left Paradise in deep trouble in the finale. And on top of all of that, Sinatra and Link’s meeting ended in one of the most jaw-dropping twists of the series… So what the heck is going on on Paradise?! What went down during that scene with Sinatra and Link, or should we say Dylan? And who or what is Alex?! Decider spoke with Julianne Nicholson, who shed some much-needed light on Season 2, Episode 7’s ending. Paradise Season 2, Episode 7 Ending Explained: “The Final Countdown” Recap Things truly started to ramp up in Paradise Season 2’s penultimate episode when Link and Sinatra finally came face to face, Sinatra handed over his requested apple pie, and the two hashed things out in a dramatic Air Force One meeting. Link compared them to Luke and Vader, because he considers Sinatra evil, while also surely foreshadowing the big twist to come. While he started by asking for one of Paradise’s modular nuclear reactors so he and his group could “restart the world,” when Sinatra called his bluff, he got down to business. “I’m here for Alex. Where is Alex?” Link said. Sinatra played dumb, but he pressed her again, clearly striking a nerve. “I think we’ve reached an impasse,” Sinatra said, standing up and leaving the plane. Link followed, but not without grabbing an Air Force One pen, which I assume will come in handy later! (Or it’s just cool!) What happened next likely made everyone watching scream “WHAT?!” at their TVs. And honestly, Paradise‘s stars were also confused when they learned of the big twist… Photo: Disney/Ser Baffo Who Is Dylan On Paradise? How Did Dylan Die? What’s With The Nosebleeds? And Is Link Sinatra’s Son?! As Link prepared to leave, Sinatra warned, “This bunker was built to sustain a nuclear blast. You won’t get in. Any attempt will only get you and your team hurt. Please forget about this and move on.” In response, Link doubled down. Hard. “Lady you’re not quite getting it, we’re coming in. I will find Alex, and we will end this,” he said. Sinatra promised to do everything in her power to protect Alex and said she wouldn’t let him destroy what she’d built. “Built? You haven’t built anything. You’ve bribed, and you’ve stolen, and you’ve killed. You’ve squeezed every last drop out of a planet that you and your fucking friends destroyed in the first place,” Link said. When his pals outside called “Link” with no response, they shouted “DYLAN, let’s go!” and we finally learned Link’s real name, which made Sinatra’s eyes go wide. Sinatra grabbed Link’s arm and asked, “Dylan? Your name is Dylan? When were you born? What’s your birthday? What’s your birthday!?” On his way out, Link removed her arm, said “May 16,” and both he and Sinatra get nosebleeds. So what the heck just happened?! Photo: Disney/Ser Baffo Sinatra thinks that Link is her late son, Dylan, who died of a mystery illness years before the the bunker was built. Earlier in the episode, Sinatra’s husband casually mentioned “Dylan would have been 26 this year,” the same age Link told Sinatra he was. When hacking Sinatra’s computer earlier, her daughter also noted the password was May 16, Dylan’s birthday. Link has the same name and birthday as Sinatra’s late son Dylan, which leads her to believe he is her son. When she goes back to her husband after the encounter, she even tells him, “It worked! I think it worked…I think [I’m OK]. I can’t explain it, but I think Dylan is, too.” Confused? Nicholson shed some light on the big twist, which she recalled finding out early in the season. “I was like, ‘Wait, how does that work?’ Physics! Quantum physics, guys! Get on board with it!” she told DECIDER. “I found it very moving. I obviously don’t know quantum physics, so I had to have faith in the writers, who did all this research. But I found it very moving, even just for Sinatra to imagine that this is her son. We don’t we don’t know, exactly. But the idea of it, and the peace it brought her, and the hopefulness was really beautiful.” As for Sinatra and Link’s nose bleeds, as noted in a prior article, they appear to happen when there’s a reverberation or change in time (more on this in a moment). They could also be a sign of temporal displacement, a time travel-y term that signifies when someone is unstuck in time, which we saw on Lost! So how is Link Sinatra’s son Dylan if Sinatra’s son died? Great question! While we don’t fully know the answer, it’s definitely related to Alex! Photo: Disney/Ser Baffo Who Is Alex In Paradise? Or Rather, What Is Alex? Since Season 2’s premiere it’s been clear that some sort of time manipulation is taking place in Paradise, and it all ties back to the mysterious Alex. In a flashback this season, scientist Dr. Louge (Geoffrey Arend) told Sinatra, “There’s only one thing that can fix this, and it’s the one thing even you can’t buy…time.” And when discussing Dylan’s death in a Season 1 flashback, Sinatra said, “Everybody said time would help. But it’s making it worse because it’s taking me further away from when he was here.” Even before the bunker, the concept of time and Dylan’s death weighed heavily on Sinatra and fueled her actions — both seen and secretive. “[Dylan’s] loss is is basically why Paradise exists. Her need to protect her remaining family has been at the top of her list ever since then. Everything is driven with that as the end goal,” Nicholson said. “I found that whole speech so moving from the first season, so to be able to return to that now and have an understanding that it never was just about the bunker, she did have a larger plan in mind from the very beginning, having little clues as to that plan working was really fun to explore.” Photo: Disney/Ser Baffo So who or what is Alex? And why is Link trying to “kill” Alex? Episode 3 revealed that Link’s former business partner/mentor, professor Henry Miller (Patrick Fischler), had a company called Vestige Quantum with technology so valuable to Sinatra that she had Billy kill him for it. Miller also had a wife named Alex, who suffered from Huntington’s Disease, and who he seemingly killed before Billy killed him. Because of Miller’s wife, viewers assumed Sinatra’s side project “Alex” was a person, but it’s increasingly likely that Alex is a codename for the advanced technology Sinatra’s using to manipulate time. I’m no quantum physicist, but quantum entanglement is the idea that “When two particles, such as a pair of photons or electrons, become entangled, they remain connected even when separated by vast distances.” And superposition deals with things existing in multiple states at once until observed. Sinatra’s side project is driving the Lost-style time travel/multiverse/causality loop-type twist. So it’s possible that multiple timelines exist at once, or perhaps she’s simply trying to go back in time and alter certain fates. Episode 6, which showed “Alex” sending warning messages about Jane’s upcoming birth to a man in 1997, suggested that Sinatra is using Alex to send messages back in time in hopes of re-shaping or tweaking the future. And Link likely knows the reverberations from those efforts can have dire consequences, so he’s trying to stop her. As a result of her work with Alex, it seems Sinatra believes her son Dylan survived — either in another timeline or as a result of alterations she made. But whether she got her quantum physics on to prevent Dylan’s death, stop the super volcano from erupting, both, or some secret fourth thing has yet to be revealed. At the end of Episode 7, Sinatra takes a secret underground tram and walks down the same hallway we saw in Xavier’s vision where he’s following Link (another example of time being shuffled). When she arrives at the restricted area that holds her secret project, she puts on a blue coat, opens the door, looks up, and says “Hi, Alex” as a warm orange glow shines down on her. At the time of writing this post, critics have only seen seven episodes of Season 2, so I have no idea what Paradise has in store either. Like viewers, I’ll be hypothesizing, brushing up on quantum physics, and counting down the days until the finale! If you haven’t already, be sure to check out some truly epic Paradise Season 2 finale teases from Nicholson, Doherty, and more stars. New episodes of Paradise premiere Mondays on Hulu.
